newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Dadas suspended after 53 pct fall.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Dadas suspended after 53 pct fall.

text.p: Shares of financial consultancy Dadas were suspended on the Ljubljana bourse on Tuesday after shedding more than 50 percent on Monday, pushing the Slovenian SBI index to a new historic low.

"Trading in Dadas was suspended because of the deep fall on Monday. Trading will resume after the company explains whether there were any changes it its business that had initiated the fall," spokeswoman of the bourse Lidija Gabrijelcic said.
Traders said Monday's drop was initiated by rumours the group's brokerage arm may be banned from trading, while the consultancy itself may face bankruptcy.

"The fall was initiated by virtually no demand for Dadas, while many investors wanted to get rid of its shares in a belief that Dadas might eventually face bankruptcy," said Sergej Racman, a trader at brokerage PM&A.
"There are several indicators that show Dadas is facing liquidity problems and will not be able to meet obligations to its creditors," he added.

Slovenia's Securities Market Agency in March started procedures to ban Dada's mutual fund Proficia Dadas its brokerage unit from trading, claiming they were rigging prices by trading among its affiliated companies.
Since then Dadas has dropped 95 percent, pulling the SBI index down as much as 42 percent. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom +386 61 125 8439
